Set up Cog

Where Cog runs

Your computer will ask for an administrator's password when you install.

Cog keeps its program, settings and everyone's files here. Pick a disk with room for them.

Admin account

The account you sign in with to manage Cog. You can add other people from the admin pages afterwards.

At least 8 characters. If Cog will be reachable from the internet, make it long.

Who can reach Cog

The plain HTTP port. With HTTPS it answers only on this computer.

Your domain

A name that points at your home's public address, such as cloud.example.com. A dynamic DNS service (Duck DNS, deSEC) gives you one for free and keeps it pointing at you when your address changes.

Let's Encrypt writes here about problems with your certificate.

Your router forwards the internet's port 443 to this one. 8443 needs no administrator rights.

How Let's Encrypt checks the name is yours

Your router forwards the internet's port 80 to this one.

The https:// address your proxy serves Cog at.

The proxy's address as a range, such as 127.0.0.1/32 or 172.16.0.0/12, so Cog sees visitors' real addresses. Separate several with commas.

To use Cog away from home later, run setup again and choose HTTPS.
